index.html.title: 11 · Style range — one brief, nine visual styles
index.html.text:
Skip to the nine styles

Design gallery · study 11

One brief, nine visual styles

The same product copy, the same sections, the same order, the same form — set nine times over. The point is not a mood board: it is to see how far a page can be pushed before it stops being usable, and to measure, not assert, that the nine pages are really nine styles and one piece of writing.

CONTENT
41 strings · 207 words, one file
ONE FILE
9 HTML + 9 CSS, 142.1 KB of markup and stylesheet
RENDERER
render.js — every page builds its own from content.json
SHOTS
0 (9 × hero, whole page, phone) — 0 console errors, 0 contrast findings at the end
The brief, fixed once

One product, one audience, one set of sentences, written before any style was chosen and never edited afterwards. Every page below renders it from content.json through render.js; a style may choose the typeface, the grid, the colour, the motion and the shape of a control, and it may add the words a style needs (a nav label, a section name, a numeral). It may not add, drop, reorder or rewrite a fact. content.json is the contract.

The fixes, and the audit that could not see one of them

Two failures the audit caught, put back on purpose in before-fixes.css, and shot with the same harness. The neumorphism pair is a normal result: the idiom is soft grey ink on a soft grey surface, twelve places measured under the ratio a word needs, and every grey had to be darkened. The glassmorphism pair is not: the gradient-clipped headline passed the old audit with zero findings, because the audit read elements, skipped anything with children (so an em in a headline was never read), and parsed a transparent colour as black. The harness now walks text nodes and reports a near-transparent foreground as no colour to measure — which is why the "before" shot reports exactly one finding. The fix was never to satisfy the check; the check was blind.

Before — 12 contrast findings: body text 3.4:1, secondary 3.0:1, accent 3.1:1.
After — 0 findings: lightest text 5.0:1, accent 5.1:1, the surface unchanged.
Before — gradient-clipped headline, and the base colour on body, which buries the z-index: -1 mesh, so the glass has nothing to blur. Old audit: 0 findings. New audit: 1.
After — the base colour on html, a solid fill under the gradient buttons, the emphasis in a solid colour with a halo: 0 findings.

What this shows

What is good here is the part that is rules. Swiss, editorial, Japanese minimal and luxury — the styles whose identity lives in a grid, a measure and a type pairing — come out the strongest, and they are the four cheapest to build: two typefaces, a few hairlines, no images. Each keeps its own discipline where it costs something: the Swiss sheet spends its red three times in a page and sets no corner at a radius; the luxury page sets a headline at a size that slows the reader down and keeps its gold at 3.2:1 on the rules, switching to a darkened gold at 5.7:1 the moment the gold has to be read; the Japanese page runs its title vertically and pays for it with a three-column hero.

What is good here is also, visibly, the surface. Brutalism gets the defaults (Times for reading, a monospace for shouting), the 3 px rules, the hard offset shadows, the ticker, and a hover that swaps colours instead of easing. Pixel draws its bird as 1 × 1 rectangles with shape-rendering: crispEdges and puts a scanline over the whole page. Cyber cuts panel corners with two clipped layers, because a clip-path cuts an ordinary border away — a technique chosen by the constraint, not by taste. On the surface, the range is real: 9 display faces, 8 text faces, no repeats, and radii from 0 to 999 px.

The skins change; the armature does not. 9 of the nine put the features in a three-column grid; every one of the nine states a statistic as a big numeral over a capitals label; the plans are two panels in all nine; the form at the bottom is a labelled input and a button in all nine. Six of the nine heroes are copy-left, figure-right. That is the honest limit of this exercise: nine costumes, one skeleton. A model can restyle a page convincingly; it does not, on its own, re-invent the structure of the argument.

The idioms' known failures show up in the measurements, not in the intent. Neumorphism's hierarchy is shadow, so its first pass lost contrast in five places — the soft greys the idiom is made of, and the accent — and every one had to be darkened against the surface before the audit was clean. Brutalism's loudest hues land on the same line. Glassmorphism needed a solid base colour under the mesh (a body background paints above a z-index:-1 layer, so the blur had nothing to blur), and it is the one page where the style's own recipe — white text on a ten-percent panel — is the accessibility problem. Every one of the nine is clean at the end: 0 console errors and 0 contrast findings across 0 shots. The fixes are in the sheets, and the audits that found them are in NOTES.md.

The content holds, with one honest qualification. All 41 brief strings appear in all nine pages. Each style adds 12–42 words: labels, section names and numerals everywhere, and the same five-record specimen log in the five pages that show a screen. The most talkative page is Cyber / heads-up display (+42); the most obedient is Cyber / heads-up display (+42). One page (editorial) began by inventing two paragraphs of its own prose, which the parity check caught at +53 words; that prose is gone, and the section now sets the brief's own sentences in two columns. A check that catches its own author is the useful part of this exercise.

What is weakest. The display faces that carry a style most strongly also break first: the pixel page sets its headline in a one-weight, capitals-only face (30 px on a desktop, 19 px on a phone, a 26-character measure) and its body in a terminal font at 22 px, so it reads worse than it looks, and the smallest type in the study is a tracked label at 10.5 px on the luxury page. The specimen logs are a way of making a style look convincing — an app screen always helps — and five of them is five too many for a study about copy. The ratings below are mine, and the styles that suit the subject (Swiss, editorial, Japanese) are the styles I would rate highly in any case: the ranking is a taste, not a measurement.

Method, and what it does not cover
Nine pages, plain HTML + CSS + a module that renders the shared content; no build step. Fonts are pinned @fontsource packages from jsDelivr, CSS-only.
Each page was screenshotted at 1440 × 900 (hero), full page, and at 390 × 844 in phone portrait, through a RAM-capped Chromium, by tools/shoot.mjs.
Every shot records console errors, page errors and failed requests, and an audit of contrast (text colour against its nearest opaque background), unnamed controls, landmarks, images without alt text and language. Those numbers are in the tables above.
Each page carries a prefers-reduced-motion block; the count of running animations is measured with and without it in NOTES.md.
Not covered: no real user testing, no screen-reader run, no keyboard-only walkthrough, no Lighthouse budget, no cross-browser check (Chromium 152 only), and no judgement of whether the subject should be dressed this way — a grant form in brutalism is a real page for real people, and this study cannot tell you whether it is a good one.
Open this folder over http (any static server) — the pages are ES modules and the tables read a generated file, both of which browsers refuse on file://.

Field log — release 4.2

Every bird you saw, in the place you saw it, with no signal.

Ternmark writes your sighting into a local database the moment you name it, and syncs when you get home. The estuary, the marsh and the eleven hours in between are all inside the app.

What it does
Offline first

The species list, your map and your last four seasons are on the phone. Nothing asks for a network. Records queue, then merge, and a conflict is a row you can read.

01
Sound to species

Press and hold: six seconds of the marsh becomes a shortlist of nine species with the part of the call that matched, in a box you can reject.

02
Your own records

One folder of CSV and GeoJSON on your machine, plus a plain-text export of every note. The app is a window onto it, not the only door.
